title: FreeSWITCH SIP MESSAGE 'api' chat-proto command execution, exploited in the wild per SignalWire, not in CISA KEV
why: SignalWire's advisory GHSA-mg63-h38w-8p9p (Oct 28) says exploitation of this path has been observed in the wild. NVD published the record on Nov 5, and Rescana and SecurityOnline both report it. Missing on Microsoft's side: it is not in CISA KEV. Rescana and SecurityOnline say it was absent on Oct 29, and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) does not include it. Not a Microsoft product.
action: Upgrade FreeSWITCH (and PBX/contact-center products that bundle it) to 1.11.3. Until then set enable-chat=false on profiles that don't need SIP chat and remove passwordless directory users. Review logs for unexpected inbound SIP MESSAGE and API activity.
product: FreeSWITCH 1.11.2 and earlier (CVE-2026-116779; fixed in 1.11.3)

title: OpenSSH 'sshhole' password-auth bypass on musl/Alpine now exploited in the wild (root on honeypot)
why: Previdian reports exploitation attempts within nine hours of CVE publication and confirmed root access on an Alpine Linux honeypot (The Hacker News, Help Net Security, Nov 6). Not in CISA KEV as of Nov 6; non-Microsoft product so MSRC n/a.
action: Upgrade to OpenSSH 10.6p2 / Alpine fixed packages and restart sshd; until then set PasswordAuthentication no, and check auth logs for password logins to '*' accounts.
product: OpenSSH sshd before 10.6p2 on musl-based Linux (Alpine, OpenWrt, Buildroot, Yocto) without PAM

title: Synology DSM NAS hit by C3RB3R (Cerber) ransomware via unauthenticated DSM flaws; Synology confirms exploitation, not in CISA KEV
why: Synology's Oct 29 notice confirms threat actors are exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 (it points to SA-24:20, CVE-2024-10441) to encrypt outdated DSM devices. Qihoo 360's Oct 29 incident analysis attributes the cases it examined to unauthenticated CVE-2026-13639/13684 (SA-26:13, Sep 18) instead, so which flaw is used is disputed. BleepingComputer (Nov 2) reports a wave of victims; Shadowserver tracks 380k+ exposed Synology NAS. Missing on Microsoft's side: none of the three CVEs appears in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed shows no Synology additions; pentest-tools lists CVE-2024-10441 as not in KEV, undated). Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 4: collector's CISA KEV feed added only WordPress CVE-2026-119977, and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 3) does not include this one, so it is still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 5: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 4) does not include it, and the collector's KEV feed added only Apple CVE-2024-27834. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Update every Synology NAS to the latest DSM build for its branch (at least 7.4-90075 / 7.3.2-86009-4 / 7.2.2-72806-9 / 7.2.1-69057-12), take DSM management ports off the internet, and search shares for .L0CK3D files and read-me3.txt.

title: Barracuda Email Security Gateway pre-auth root RCE chain (CVE-2026-116606 + CVE-2026-111560): watchTowr publishes full chain and detection generator
why: On Nov 5 watchTowr Labs published the full unauthenticated-to-root chain: a failed password change that keeps going, then a crafted config-backup restore (the checksum secret is hardcoded) that injects through the timezone field. They also released a Detection Artefact Generator on GitHub. THN, BleepingComputer and SecurityWeek covered it. No exploitation has been reported yet, and ESG was hit by UNC4841 zero-days in 2023. Missing on Microsoft's side: it is not in CISA KEV. ThreatDefence checked on Nov 4, and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (Nov 5) does not include it. Not a Microsoft product.
action: Confirm that ESG firmware is 9.4.0.030 or later (patch BNSF-40425 or BNSF-40430) and that the other Barracuda appliances have their patch IDs applied. Block the admin interface from the internet now that exploit details are public.
product: Barracuda Email Security Gateway before 9.4.0.030 (bypass + root chain). The command injection alone also affects Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, WAF and Web Security Gateway (patch IDs only)

title: Refrigeration-controller sabotage wave widens: French blood-bank plasma freezers (EFS/Coolworld) set to 110°C after supermarket attacks in BE/SE/FR and more
why: New wave: NL Times (Nov 2) reports at least dozens of Delhaize stores, butcher De Laet & Van Haver and 15 Carrefour Belgium stores hit late Nov 1/early Nov 2, and Swedish media report ICA stores with cooling at 50°C overnight (HN discussion, Sweden Herald). Same pattern as the Oct 11-12 French campaign (CERT-FR CERTFR-2026-ALE-012: numerous compromised Danfoss AK-SM/AK-SC controllers). A public PoC for the Danfoss 'code of the day' auth bypass CVE-2025-41450 has been on GitHub since Oct 13. CISA's KEV file listed no Danfoss entry as of Oct 12 and none appear in KEV additions Oct 25-31; no authority has confirmed which flaw is used (the CVE link is inference). Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 4: collector's CISA KEV feed added only WordPress CVE-2026-119977, and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 3) does not include this one, so it is still not in KEV. Change Nov 4: the wave reached French Blood Establishment (EFS) plasma cold stores. Their refrigeration provider Coolworld blamed a third-party component, and setpoints were raised to 110°C (Nov 1-2); alarms caught it before anything was lost (NBC/AP, CNBC, France 24). Reports list at least six more countries. Investigators have not named a controller model or CVE, so the Danfoss link is still inference. Not in KEV (Senserva KEV-7d, Nov 4). Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Take every refrigeration/building controller off the public internet now (contractor access only via VPN with MFA), upgrade AK-SM 8xxA to R4.3.1+, plan replacement of EOL AK-SM 800/AK-SC 355, and check setpoints and defrost schedules against baseline.
product: Danfoss AK-SM 800A / AK-SM 8xxA System Manager before R4.3.1 (auth bypass fixed in R4.2), end-of-life AK-SM 800 and AK-SC 355; Copeland/Dixell XWEB controllers

title: Cisco Secure Email Gateway unauthenticated SQLi-to-root RCE: public Metasploit module, not in KEV
why: Rapid7's Metasploit release (Nov 6) adds an unauthenticated SQLi-to-root RCE module for Secure Email Gateway that Rapid7 believes maps to CVE-2026-76443. Sibling CVEs 76461 and 76519 are in KEV; 76443 itself is not in KEV and has no reported in-the-wild use.
action: Confirm every Secure Email Gateway/SEWM runs a fixed build (15.5.5-014 / 16.5.0-780 or later) and restrict management interfaces to trusted hosts.
product: Cisco Secure Email Gateway and Secure Email and Web Manager (AsyncOS) 15.5 and earlier

affected.product: Cisco AsyncOS for Secure Email Gateway

title: NIKKE PC launcher supply-chain attack: tampered Level Infinite CDN scripts delivered a remote-access/credential-stealing agent to Windows players
why: The publisher confirmed on X on Nov 4 that a third party tampered with the launcher's script files and pushed a client fix. Independent analyses (MotherSphere, WormW on GitHub) and BleepingComputer, CyberInsider and Inven describe a LuaJIT RAT plus a Chrome-loaded DLL that steals browser passwords, cookies, SSH keys, API tokens and wallet data. The analysis says some Microsoft Defender Offline scans missed the per-victim DLL. There is no CISA KEV entry, CVE or Microsoft advisory. Rechecked Nov 5: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 4) does not include it, and the collector's KEV feed added only Apple CVE-2024-27834. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Search endpoints for 'k2f_chan' in NIKKE\Launcher\intl_service\debug.log and for 'k2f.agent' in %APPDATA%\nikke_launcher\tbs_cache. On any hit, reimage the machine, then rotate browser-saved passwords, session cookies, SSH keys and API tokens from a clean device.
product: Goddess of Victory: NIKKE PC launcher (launches roughly Oct 23/24 - Nov 4, 2026, before the Nov 4 client fix)

title: Zyxel GS1900 switches: zero-day used in attacks on ~1,000 switches bypasses the KEV-listed CVE-2026-7273 patch; new CVE-2026-107441 is not in KEV
why: Binarly recovered the attackers' 'GS1900 Pre-Auth RCE' exploit from Red Heron/JITTERLY infrastructure and showed that it still works without changes on all 10 Patch 2 builds that were released to fix KEV-listed CVE-2026-7273. GreyNoise had reported 996 switches looted around Aug 17. Zyxel shipped Patch 3 on Oct 22 and published the advisory on Nov 3 (BleepingComputer, THN, SecurityOnline). CISA's KEV catalog lists only the old CVE-2026-7273; THN notes CVE-2026-107441 is not in KEV. It is unclear how many of the 996 victims fell to the new bug, and the vendor does not confirm exploitation. Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade every GS1900 switch to the 2.90(.3)C0 firmware for its model, move the web management interface onto a management VLAN, and treat any exposed switch as compromised: rotate its root/admin passwords and review its configuration.
product: Zyxel GS1900 series switches (10 models) on firmware 2.90(xxxx.2)C0 and earlier, i.e. including the June 'Patch 2' fix for CVE-2026-7273; fixed in 2.90(xxxx.3)C0

title: DreamHost File Manager breach: an undisclosed third-party software flaw was exploited from Aug to Oct 23, exposing FTP/SFTP passwords and webmail sessions
why: DreamHost's breach notice (filed with the California AG; BleepingComputer, TechCrunch and gbhackers, Nov 4) says an attacker exploited a vulnerability in the third-party software behind its File Manager from about August 2026 until Oct 23. The attacker stole FTP/SFTP credentials and some webmail credentials and session tokens. The software and the flaw have not been named, so other hosts running the same file manager cannot yet check themselves. No CVE, nothing in KEV, and not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: If you host sites on DreamHost, rotate FTP/SFTP and mailbox passwords (and any reused elsewhere), diff site files against a known-good copy for injected code, and remove unknown mailbox forwarding rules.
product: DreamHost web-based File Manager (files.dreamhost.com) and webmail; the exploited third-party File Manager software is unnamed

title: Control Web Panel: CWPdoor trojanized cwpsrv backdoor found on real servers, as public exploit for CWP2Shell root RCE chain lands
why: XLab (via BleepingComputer, Nov 5) found CWPdoor, a trojanized cwpsrv, with real victims; VulnCheck published a working go-exploit module for the CWP2Shell unauthenticated-to-root chain (disclosed Nov 2). None of these CVEs is in CISA KEV. How CWPdoor gets installed is unknown, and the CWP2Shell flaws have no confirmed in-the-wild use yet. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade CWP to the latest release (1.29+/1.30), restrict port 2083/2087/2031 to admin networks, and run XLab's triage checks for a trojanized cwpsrv (socket, process and binary-string checks listed in the BleepingComputer report); if positive, replace the binary and rotate all panel credentials.
product: Control Web Panel (CWP7) webpanel before 1.29 (CWP2Shell chain); cwpsrv binary replaced by CWPdoor on compromised hosts

title: CryptoPayment Gateway WordPress plugin: unpatched unauthenticated admin-action flaw (CVSS 10.0) exposing wallet credentials now under exploitation attempts
why: Defused Cyber reported in-the-wild exploitation attempts (starting Nov 2) from 'KYC-free VPS' infrastructure; The Hacker News covered it Nov 3. WPScan says no fix exists. Not in CISA KEV (OpenCVE; collector KEV feed shows no additions). Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 4: collector's CISA KEV feed added only WordPress CVE-2026-119977, and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 3) does not include this one, so it is still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 5: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 4) does not include it, and the collector's KEV feed added only Apple CVE-2024-27834. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Remove the CryptoPayment Gateway plugin from any WordPress site, rotate the wallet keys it stored, and audit for deleted files or changed gateway settings.
product: CryptoPayment Gateway WordPress plugin 1.2.1 through 1.2.2 (no fix; plugin closed on WordPress.org since Aug 28, 2026)

title: CPython sandbox-escape 0-day disclosed by RunSybil; upstream treated it as a bug, not a security issue
why: On Nov 5, oss-security relayed RunSybil's blog on a CPython sandbox escape. RunSybil could not get it handled as a security vulnerability, so it submitted fix PR #155761, and upstream is not backporting it to security releases. A downstream review (MaplePrivacyLabs PR #1409) mentions a RunSybil Jinja sandbox-escape demonstration and a CPython GenericAlias out-of-bounds read (cpython#155752) first guarded in 3.14.8. No CVE, no advisory, not in CISA KEV. Not a Microsoft product.
action: Don't treat Jinja SandboxedEnvironment or other in-process Python sandboxes as a security boundary for untrusted input. Isolate them in a container or VM, and move 3.14 runtimes to the latest 3.14.x.
product: CPython (affected versions unconfirmed; one downstream review cites a GenericAlias out-of-bounds read guarded from 3.14.8)

title: Copeland/Dixell XWEB PRO refrigeration controllers hijacked into an SMTP botnet
why: SecurityScorecard STRIKE (OTX pulse, Nov 6) found a suspected SMTP botnet including confirmed XWEB PRO controllers, citing unpatched CVE-2026-25085. Not in CISA KEV; CISA SSVC still lists exploitation 'none'.
action: Take XWEB controllers off the public internet (VPN-only), update to the latest Copeland firmware, and check for unexpected outbound SMTP from OT networks.
product: XWEB 300D PRO / 500D PRO / 500B PRO firmware 1.12.1 and earlier

title: Chainstack production breach (customer data, password hashes, node credentials) tied to ARTEX AI-agent intrusion campaign also hitting WorkOS and Chainalysis
why: Chainstack disclosed on Nov 3 that an attacker entered through a third-party component on Oct 26, reached production and a database of customer names, emails and password hashes, and could access systems holding node credentials (The Hacker News, Mallory). The Hacker News links it to the ARTEX autonomous-agent campaign (China-linked cluster) that also breached WorkOS and Chainalysis; that attribution is an assessment, not confirmed by Chainstack. No CVE, so nothing in CISA KEV; no Microsoft report on ARTEX seen. Change Nov 4: Hunt.io published a report on the ARTEX infrastructure tied to the seven South Korean financial-institution breaches (OTX pulse). Still a SaaS breach, so no KEV or MSRC entry applies. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: If you use Chainstack, change account passwords, rotate all node credentials and regenerate platform API keys now, and review node/API usage since Oct 26.
product: Chainstack blockchain node platform (console accounts, node credentials, platform API keys)

title: Rails Active Storage ImageMagick unauthenticated arbitrary file write/read (CVE-2026-122006, CVSS 9.8)
why: On Nov 4 Rails published GHSA-f3w6-w445-fwh9, now CVE-2026-122006: an uploaded crafted file can write arbitrary files and, with the Disk service, read secret_key_base. THN and Ostorlab covered it. No public exploit and not in CISA KEV (HOL Guard, Nov 4). Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 5: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 4) does not include it, and the collector's KEV feed added only Apple CVE-2024-27834. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade to Rails 8.1.4.1 or 8.0.5.2 (with mini_magick 5.1 or later). Confirm the shipped ImageMagick policy loads, and move 7.2 or older apps to a supported series.
product: activestorage before 8.0.5.2 and 8.1.x before 8.1.4.1 (apps using ImageMagick/mini_magick)

title: Android Framework zero-click RCE (CVE-2026-58868) in November 2026 bulletin, Android 14-17
why: Google rates CVE-2026-58868 Critical: a heap overflow in FrameDecoder.cpp that allows remote code execution with no user interaction (November bulletin, THN, Security Affairs, Rescana). It is not in CISA KEV (Nov 3 catalog). Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 5: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 4) does not include it, and the collector's KEV feed added only Apple CVE-2024-27834. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Use MDM to flag Android devices below security patch level 2026-11-01 (2026-11-05 covers the whole bulletin), and set a deadline to update or replace them.
product: Android 14, 15, 16, 16 QPR2, 17 (before security patch level 2026-11-01)

title: Trojanized ARTEX AI pentest Docker image (tomicdd/artex) gives unauthenticated root shell; 62 exposed consoles; CERT-In flags Crafty Falcon
why: BadByte analysis (Nov 4) and The Hacker News (Nov 5) document a backdoor in a widely pulled ARTEX Docker image (~9,000 pulls, 62 internet consoles serving it Nov 2-4). No CVE, vendor advisory or CISA KEV entry exists (Ostorlab, Nov 5). Use of the backdoor against those consoles has not been reported. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Search container hosts and registries for tomicdd/artex or congdonglinux/artex; stop and preserve any such container, rebuild from reviewed source only, and rotate every secret the container could read.
product: tomicdd/artex and congdonglinux/artex Docker images (backdoored copies of ARTEX v0.3.15)

title: DigiCert breach: internet-exposed archive system leaked customer contacts and some ID documents (passports, licences)
why: DigiCert breach notification and Mozilla Bugzilla incident report (BleepingComputer, Nov 5) confirm unauthorized read access to archived validation data via a self-registration flaw after a Feb 2025 migration. This is a vendor breach, not a patchable CVE: there is no KEV entry and nothing for Defender to detect. The main risk is phishing that impersonates certificate validation. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Identify which of your staff submitted organization/identity validation documents to DigiCert, warn them, and treat 're-upload your ID / validation failed' messages claiming to be DigiCert as phishing; no certificate reissue is needed.
product: DigiCert internal archived-customer-data business system (CA services, CertCentral, DigiCert ONE reported unaffected)

title: Chainalysis breach: 'offensive agentic' intrusion exposed password hashes and live tokens for all users; KYT/Reactor offline
why: In its Nov 4 update Chainalysis said names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all users were exposed. It also reported an on-path attack that captured some passwords and some KYT accounts accessed without authorization. The Record, The Register, THN and American Banker all report it. The vulnerability and actor have not been disclosed, so there is nothing for KEV or Microsoft to track yet, and no detection guidance exists.
action: If your organization uses Chainalysis, rotate its API keys and passwords (and any reused elsewhere), revoke integrations that hold Chainalysis tokens, and review KYT/API activity since October for unauthorized use.
product: Chainalysis Reactor, KYT, Address Screening, Data Solutions (hosted)

title: Sogou Input Method for Windows exploited in the wild: SlippyNunchucks hijacks HTTP config to deploy DarkVigil
why: ESET reports a China-aligned group (SlippyNunchucks) has exploited SGTool.exe's plain-HTTP config retrieval since July 1, 2026. It redirects DNS for the Sogou config host and delivers the DarkVigil/FDMTP implant to victims in six countries (THN, Infosecurity, NVD Nov 4). Not in CISA KEV (TheHackerWire). Not a Microsoft product, so no MSRC advisory applies. Rechecked Nov 5: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 4) does not include it, and the collector's KEV feed added only Apple CVE-2024-27834. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Inventory Windows endpoints running Sogou Input Method and update them to 16.10 or later, or remove it. Hunt for unexpected DLLs written by SGTool.exe.
product: Sogou Input Method for Windows before 16.10

title: ManageEngine Log360 / EventLog Analyzer unauthenticated unauthorized-access flaw (CVSS 9.1) fixed after build 13062
why: Zoho published the CVE and fix on Nov 3 (CVSS 9.1, AV:N/PR:N); details are withheld. No PoC or exploitation reported and not in CISA KEV (TheHackerWire; collector KEV feed). ManageEngine products have a history of KEV-listed auth bypasses. Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 4: collector's CISA KEV feed added only WordPress CVE-2026-119977, and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 3) does not include this one, so it is still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 5: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 4) does not include it, and the collector's KEV feed added only Apple CVE-2024-27834. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade Log360 and EventLog Analyzer to the build after 13062 named in Zoho's advisory and restrict the web console to admin networks.
product: ManageEngine Log360 and EventLog Analyzer builds 13062 and below

title: Cisco ISE / ISE-PIC unauthenticated authorization bypass lets attackers obtain an endpoint identity certificate
why: Cisco PSIRT published this on Nov 4: an unauthenticated remote attacker can obtain an endpoint identity certificate from ISE with a crafted request. No exploitation or PoC reported, and not in CISA KEV (Senserva KEV-7d, Nov 4). Rechecked Nov 5: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 4) does not include it, and the collector's KEV feed added only Apple CVE-2024-27834. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Check the Cisco advisory for fixed ISE releases and patch. Restrict access to ISE interfaces with infrastructure ACLs until then.
product: Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE) and ISE Passive Identity Connector

title: Apache OFBiz before 24.09.08: second pre-auth RCE CVE-2026-83542 (CVSS 9.8) joins 68524/73578 in 46-CVE batch
why: NVD published CVE-2026-83542 (unauthenticated Groovy code injection, also reachable via the unauthenticated /sfa/control/editPortalPageColumnWidth route) on Nov 5. Ostorlab and OffSeq report it is not in CISA KEV and no exploitation is known; OFBiz has a KEV history. No public PoC seen. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade every OFBiz instance to 24.09.08 and restrict the web UI to admin networks until done.
product: Apache OFBiz all releases before 24.09.08 (no 18.12 backports)

title: Keycloak SAML HTTP-Redirect signature bypass (CVSS 9.1): unauthenticated takeover of federated accounts
why: Red Hat CVE published Nov 5 (CVSS 9.1, pre-auth); a Sploitus entry exists but no verified public exploit, and it is not in CISA KEV. Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Apply the Red Hat/Keycloak fix for CVE-2026-117691; until then block SAML redirect-binding requests with percent-encoded SAMLResponse/SAMLRequest parameter names at the WAF and review SAML broker logins.
product: Keycloak / Red Hat build of Keycloak (SAML HTTP-Redirect binding); fixed versions not yet stated in our sources

title: Craft CMS unauthenticated SQL injection in element search (admin takeover)
why: VulnCheck/GHSA advisory published Nov 6 for an unauthenticated stacked-query SQLi (CVSS 9.3/9.8); no exploit or in-the-wild use seen yet. Not in CISA KEV.
action: Upgrade Craft CMS to 4.18.9 or 5.11.2.

title: Xen XSA-523 grant-copy flaws let a malicious guest read/write any domain's memory including dom0
why: Xen published XSA-523 on Nov 3 (found by Anthropic with Claude, validated by Ada Logics): any guest can read and write other domains' memory, including dom0, with no known mitigation. XCP-ng and Qubes shipped fixes, but Debian bookworm/trixie were still vulnerable on Nov 4. No exploitation reported and not in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 5: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 4) does not include it, and the collector's KEV feed added only Apple CVE-2024-27834. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Apply the XSA-523 patches or your vendor's Xen update (XCP-ng xen-4.17.7-4.2.xcpng8.3, Qubes 4.19.6-3) and reboot hosts that run untrusted guests.
product: Xen 4.6 and later (patches for 4.17-4.19 and unstable); XCP-ng, Qubes OS

title: FreeRDP 3.32.2 fixes 15 memory-safety flaws (CVSS up to 9.3): proxy OOB write, client UAFs, RD Gateway overflow
why: NVD published 15 FreeRDP CVEs on Nov 4, fixed in 3.32.2. They include an out-of-bounds write in freerdp-proxy reachable by any connecting client (9.3) and client use-after-frees triggered by malicious RDP servers (9.3). No PoC or exploitation reported, and not in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 5: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 4) does not include it, and the collector's KEV feed added only Apple CVE-2024-27834. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Update FreeRDP to 3.32.2 (and distro packages that bundle it), and prioritise any internet-reachable freerdp-proxy or shadow server.
product: FreeRDP before 3.32.2 (client, proxy, shadow server)

title: SonicWall GMS 9.5.2 and earlier: unauthenticated internal file read (CVSS 9.1) + post-auth SQLi CVE-2026-109594, no patch coming (EOL)
why: SonicWall advisory SNWLID-2026-0019 (Nov 3) discloses an unauthenticated internal file read (CVSS 9.1) and says no fix will be released because GMS is end-of-life. BleepingComputer, SecurityOnline and VulDB covered it on Nov 4. No exploitation or public exploit is reported, and it is not in CISA KEV. CISA has listed 19 SonicWall flaws in KEV over four years. Nov 5: The Hacker News also covered it; still no fix and not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Take GMS off any untrusted network now (management VLAN or admin IP allowlist only) and plan a migration to SonicWall NSM.
product: SonicWall Global Management System (GMS) 9.5.2 and earlier (end-of-life; no fix will be released, migrate to NSM)

title: Windows Paint RCE CVE-2026-83844 goes viral; the fixed build is unclear and not reaching many PCs
why: Not ahead: MSRC published it on Oct 13 (Important, CVSS 8.1, AC:H, exploitation less likely). No public PoC or in-the-wild use has been reported, and it is not in CISA KEV. The news this week is chatter (HN 525 points) and confusion over the fixed build: MSRC moved it from 11.2605.91.0 to 11.2609.401.0, and the Store still serves older builds in places.
action: Check the installed version with Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.Paint, aim for 11.2609.401.0 or later, and remove Paint where nobody uses it.
product: Microsoft Paint before 11.2609.401.0 (MSRC current; CVE record still says 11.2605.91.0)

title: Apache Axis 1.x (EOL) unauthenticated remote class instantiation via SOAP fault: no fix
why: Apache disclosed a critical, unauthenticated flaw on oss-security (Nov 6) in an unsupported library still embedded in many Java products; no released fix. Not in CISA KEV.
action: Inventory Java apps and appliances bundling axis-1.x jars and plan migration; restrict network access to SOAP endpoints that act as Axis 1.x clients/servers.
product: Apache Axis 1.x through 1.4 (end of life)

title: Debian/Ubuntu APT man-in-the-middle package swap after verification gives root code execution (DSA-6607-1)
why: Debian DSA-6607-1 (Nov 4, found by Max Justicz): an on-path attacker, such as a malicious mirror or proxy, can swap a package after APT verifies it and get code execution as root. Covered by HN, Phoronix and Mallory. No public PoC or exploitation, and not in CISA KEV. Nov 4: reposted to oss-security; still no PoC and not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 6: Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 5) lists only Apple CVE-2024-27834, WordPress 119977, Ivanti 111357/118527, Cisco 76418 and GitLab 97229, and the collector's KEV feed added nothing, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Update apt (3.0.4 trixie / 2.6.2 bookworm / Ubuntu USN), and use HTTPS mirrors; avoid apt over untrusted networks until patched.
product: APT on Debian 12/13, Ubuntu 22.04+ and derivatives (Acquire::Retries non-zero, default since bookworm/jammy)

title: D-Link DGS-3130 switches: multiple unpatched DDP zero-days (no CVEs yet)
why: D-Link published mitigations (BleepingComputer, Nov 6) for unpatched D-Link Discovery Protocol flaws; no CVE, no patch, no exploitation reported. Not in CISA KEV.
action: Disable DDP, remove default SNMP communities, and restrict SSH/web/SNMP management to an isolated management network.
product: DGS-3130 series (DGS-3130-30TS, multiple firmware versions)
